title: Multimodal neural fusion distinguishes tissue states in a small preclinical imaging cohort
summary: A two-branch neural network combined Raman spectra and optical-coherence images to distinguish dysplasia/cancer from control tissue. Animal-separated evaluation in a small longitudinal cohort reported 92.3% pooled accuracy. This is preclinical feasibility, not clinical diagnostic accuracy.
ai_technology: Multimodal convolutional neural network; ResNet-18; Grad-CAM

evidence.tested: Fivefold animal-independent evaluation used 196 paired observations from 11 mice. Every contributing animal was withheld once.
evidence.unknown: Small exploratory cohort; early-stopping validation partition is incompletely specified. Measurements used externally positioned tissue rather than deployed endoscopy. Pooled and fold-average metrics differ. No human screening, earlier diagnosis or treatment benefit is demonstrated.
evidence.ai_role: Learned spectral and image representations are fused for the specific pathology-reference classification.

source_review.scope: Primary front tuple and safe computational fusion/evaluation Methods and nonactionable classification Results; animal procedures excluded.
